item.title: Mood Machine – Liz Pelly
item.description: The dark side of streaming exposed! This week we're bringing the chill vibes in the form of an algorithmically generated playlist. First they came for the low-fi beats, but we're speaking out.
item.content:encoded:
How do Spotify's algorithms shape our listening habits? How much AI-generated PFC has secretly been snuck into our daily diet, and what's the real cost of the perfect playlist? This week we're putting on our headphones and listening properly for once, in a dark room. The streaming figures are in, but those 0.001 pennies aren't adding up.

This week's book: Mood Machine by Liz Pelly (2025)

Further reading: How Music Got Free by Stephen Witt (2015) Perfect Sound Whatever by James Acaster (2019) Black Vinyl, White Powder by Simon Napier-Bell (2001) Information Doesn't Want to Be Free by Cory Doctorow (2014) How Music Works by David Byrne (2012)

item.title: If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies – Eliezer Yudkowsky
item.description: The end of the world could only be a few megabytes away! This week superhuman AI might kill us all, so listen now before it's too late.
item.content:encoded:
What happens if AI reaches the level of super intelligence? Very bad things! At least according to Eliezer Yudkowsky, and this is the premise of his book. The hominid god looks down kindly on this latest episode of Your Cover's Blown.

This week's book: If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies by Eliezer Yudkowsky (2025)

item.title: Kitchen Confidential – Anthony Bourdain
item.description: Secrets from the kitchen exposed! This week we're ordering fish on a Monday.
item.content:encoded:
Anthony Bourdain was a famous chef and travel writer. We're returning to where it all began with his tell all memoir Kitchen Confidential. Welcome to Your Cover's Blown, the podcast where we order fish on Mondays.

This week's book: Kitchen Confidential by Anthony Bourdain (2000)

item.title: Never Split the Difference – Chris Voss
item.description: An ex-FBI hostage negotiator teaches you how to get your way at work, at home and at the car dealership. This week we're learning to negotiate like a hostage.
item.content:encoded:
Chris Voss was an FBI negotiator and his book contains many practical examples of applying the techniques he learned in everyday life. The downward inflecting DJ voice, mirroring and many other techniques will be studied. All this and more in the first episode of Your Cover's Blown, a reverse yes-ladder of a podcast that will have you uncontrollably exclaiming "That's right!" before the hour is through.

This week's book: Never Split the Difference by Chris Voss (2016)
